blockers.title: The UTF-8 OptionalData rule is not the Linux EFI-stub command-line ABI
evidence: v34 correctly defines how to locate the opaque OptionalData suffix of EFI_LOAD_OPTION, but then declares that suffix to be a UTF-8 Linux EFI-stub command line and searches its raw bytes for ASCII tokens.

The Linux EFI-stub LoadOptions command-line ABI consumes CHAR16/UTF-16 code units, not an un-terminated UTF-8 byte string. A correctly encoded token such as lockdown=integrity therefore contains a zero byte after each ASCII character and cannot satisfy v34's UTF-8 tokenization rule.

The converse also fails: raw UTF-8 bytes that satisfy v34's OptionalData matcher are not the corresponding CHAR16 command line when the EFI stub consumes them. The resulting effective command line cannot be assumed to contain either required token, so the kernel is not caused to select integrity lockdown or the sysctl command-line setting by the measured bytes.

Requiring /proc/cmdline to contain the two tokens does not repair the carrier mismatch. A conforming UTF-16 EFI-stub boot is rejected by the raw OptionalData rule, while a raw UTF-8 load option accepted by that rule is not the command line the directly launched Linux EFI stub interprets.

Linux remains mandatory in D-002 slice 1. A profile whose authenticated carrier encoding is incompatible with the named direct-launch ABI is an effective Linux qualification failure, not a valid platform-removal path.
blockers.impact: The only new evidence claimed to establish pre-userspace no-replacement is not delivered to the authenticated Linux kernel in the defined form. Correct direct EFI-stub boots cannot satisfy the contract as written, and bytes accepted by the contract do not establish the asserted lockdown/kexec policy.
blockers.requiredRepair: Specify the actual Linux EFI-stub LoadOptions encoding and length/termination rules (CHAR16/UTF-16 as applicable), retain and authenticate the exact raw EFI_LOAD_OPTION bytes, decode them deterministically, and prove that the decoded command line delivered to K contains the closed required-token set. Add positive and negative vectors for raw load-option bytes, decoding, duplicates, malformed code units, and the resulting /proc/cmdline.

blockers.title: Current-kernel self-reports do not prove that authenticated K disabled kexec before userspace
evidence: The TPM quote, event log, BootCurrent, Boot#### VariableData, and kernelEvent authenticate the firmware launch of allowlisted K. v34's own inScopeBootConfigs still correctly states that this evidence does not authenticate a later kexec or other post-boot kernel replacement.

The new /proc/cmdline, /sys/kernel/security/lockdown, /proc/sys/kernel/kexec_load_disabled, and optional kexec_loaded observations are all read from whichever kernel is current at observation time. No field cryptographically or temporally joins those observations to K before any initramfs or userspace code ran.

The role sentence asserts that the measured option disables kexec before userspace, but the signed inventory and authenticatedKernelMember carry no required capability stating that exact K implements the sysctl.* command-line handler with the required early ordering. effectiveCmdline requires only token presence in the current command line, not equality to the measured OptionalData decoded as K's effective command line.

Concrete counterexample: allowlisted K does not apply sysctl.kernel.kexec_load_disabled=1 from its load options before userspace. Privileged early userspace stages a different signed M while kexec remains enabled, writes K's one-way load-disable value after staging, and enters M with a command line containing both required tokens. M can select integrity, report kexec_load_disabled=1, and report kexec_loaded=0 because no image is staged in M. A fresh quote still authenticates the original firmware launch of K. Every v34 present-state check can pass although undeclared M supplies the live OS ABI.

The optional build-id detector cannot close this counterexample, runtimeContinuity remains explicitly non-governing, and G22 is NAMED-NOT-QUALIFIED. NT-TCB-KEXEC checks only the measured token bytes and current symptoms; it contains no observation of the pre-userspace transition at which the policy must become irreversible.

Thus the PTCB-V33-B1 signed-replacement counterexample is narrowed only for kernels already known to honor the early parameter. v34 neither binds nor proves that prerequisite, so it still admits a false allow for an authenticated K that lacks or does not execute that early handler.
blockers.impact: A qualification can authenticate K while observing compliant values from a different signed M. The actual OS-ABI TCB remains open, violating the exact signed-entry identity rule, NT-TCB-1, and the hostile-clean-machine requirement.
blockers.requiredRepair: Bind authenticatedKernelMember to a qualified, signed capability rule for the exact early command-line handler and its ordering before all user-controlled initramfs/userspace, prove exact equality between authenticated OptionalData and K's effective command line, and retain event-bound evidence that the one-way disable took effect before any image could be staged. Alternatively authenticate the currently executing kernel independently and compare its exact cryptographic identity to the signed OS-ABI inventory. Present current-kernel self-reports alone are insufficient.

shouldFix.title: The new loader option is impossible under the unchanged classMap
evidence: Every signed entry must carry an identityEvidence tag allowed by classMap for its class.

preKernelReferences.join requires every non-kernel code-bearing row's signedEntry to use DIGEST-BOUND. classForCodeRows now says that entry's class MUST be loader or comparable system-class dependency.

classMap allows DIGEST-BOUND for comparable system-class dependency, but allows loader only as PLATFORM-ATTESTED. Therefore no conforming four-field signedEntry can simultaneously have class loader and satisfy the mandatory DIGEST-BOUND join.

Relabeling every actual loader as comparable system-class dependency avoids the syntactic collision only by discarding the contract's declared loader taxonomy. The claimed PTCB-V33-ADV1 repair consequently leaves one branch of its new rule dead and classifiers can diverge between false refusal and misclassification.
shouldFix.impact: A legitimate pre-kernel loader row has no lawful identity-evidence form under the combined rules, so independent implementations cannot produce the same closed signed inventory and trace decision.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Either add a class-appropriate DIGEST-BOUND route for loader in classMap and roster that change, or remove loader from classForCodeRows and define why all such measured firmware/application rows are correctly classified as comparable system-class dependency. Do not require a DIGEST-BOUND loader while globally forbidding that tag for loader.

verdictBasis: REJECT because ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX; this review finds 2 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX finding.
conclusion: REJECT. v34 reproduces its custody pins, keeps Linux in D-002 slice 1, closes the scope-enumeration omission, and makes NT-TCB-KEXEC fail-closed in prose. It does not supply a valid Linux EFI-stub carrier: the raw OptionalData rule is UTF-8 while the named load-options ABI is CHAR16/UTF-16. Even with that corrected, current-kernel command-line and sysctl self-reports do not prove that authenticated K made the one-way kexec setting before userspace; a late-stage/late-disable/signed-M transition can still pass. The pre-kernel loader repair also conflicts with classMap. DR-126 remains OPEN; no DR is marked SATISFIED, and no D-096 (A) grant, application, sealing, or implementation authority is created.
